text:
alex: Hey - CI flagged a microbench regression on PR #20456, threshold +12% on kernel selection path. This looks like the kernel autoselect changed preference for long-ctx kernels.

ci-bot: @alex CI results: microbench/text-gen-kernels: baseline=1.00ms, PR=1.12ms (12%). Threshold=5%. Full log: https://ci/reports/20456/microbench.txt :warning:

sophia: Ugh. I saw this locally too when running with seq=1024 samples. KV cache hit-rate drops during warmup.

kevin: Can you paste the perf summary / flamegraph?

perf-bot: Flamegraph attached (snippet):
```
# Flamegraph top
kernel_select_choose()  45%
quant_path_long()      20%
batch_scheduler_wait() 10%
kv_cache_lookup()      8%
```

alex: Looks like the autoselect now biases toward the 'long' kernel after the scheduler change in the PR. That increases register pressure => slightly slower per-token on common short sequences, and warms KV cache differently.

sophia: I ran a quick bisect across the merge window: bad commit is 6f3b9d2 (scheduler: prefer fewer, larger batches heuristics). Repro script:
```
./tools/run_microbench --model=xl --seq=1024 --profile --repeat=100
```

jordan: This landed late in the release patchset; it's blocking the canary rollout IMO. I recommend holding canary until we have a fix or a revert. :hand:

kevin: I'll open a revert PR for the scheduler heuristic change (wip). If we can't fix fast we should revert.

alex: Before we revert, can we try a hotfix to autoselect thresholds? Maybe cap long-kernel score when seq distribution is short. Quick patch idea: clamp long_kernel_score = min(long_kernel_score, 1.1).

sophia: I instrumented the kernel selector with a small probe. With clamp=1.1 the microbench delta goes down to +1.8%, within threshold. Running full CI now.

ci-bot: New CI run queued for PR 20456-hotfix (job 8792).

perf-bot: Microbench unit diff (hotfix branch): baseline=1.00ms, hotfix=1.018ms (1.8%) - PASS threshold.

kevin: Nice. I'll hold the revert. Please add a regression test for preferential bias so autoselect doesn't flip on scheduler heuristic changes.

alex: Agree. Added test + comment. Also adding a short-note in the release notes about kernel autoselect sensitivity.

jordan: OK to proceed with canary if hotfix branch passes end-to-end and perf guardrails are green. I'll schedule the gated rollout for tomorrow morning.

sophia: TL;DR: root cause = scheduler heuristic changed batch shape -> kernel autoselect picked long-path -> KV warmup + register pressure -> CI microbench threshold hit. Hotfix = clamp autoselect bias -> fixes perf; follow-ups = regression test + longer-term: make selector robust to transient batch-shape shifts.

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll post a short postmortem in #postmortems after rollout. :thumbsup:
